data.title: What is Ethereum actually for? A judge and Vitalik Buterin both left it open
data.description:
the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

What was the case about?

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

The government called the prosecution,

The very first of its kind.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

She continued,

It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

What are crypto’s varying use cases?

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

He also wrote,

Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior… We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

Is crypto unequivalent to TradFi?

The three developments have been framing crypto’s developing role separately, but these assets have a long way to go before they can fully replace TradFi.

Vitalik Buterin himself leaves the question open, as he observed,

We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The ruling did not answer that question, nor did the outage.

Final Summary

  • A federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in a “first of its kind” wire fraud case over a $25M Ethereum exploit, finding that there was no material misrepresentation.
  • The same day, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley urged users to hold stablecoins amid major U.S. bank outages, and Vitalik Buterin said digital assets still lack housing’s “safe, non-crazy” default properties.

data.title: Dumping to stacking in just three months? What’s going on with XRP whales?
data.description:
XRP’s price dipped under $1, and most of the market looks ready to walk away. Not the whales, though. At least not yet.

Is that enough to stop the fall?

Whales are pulling their stash off Binance!

According to recent data, XRP whales have taken out more than $127 million in XRP off Binance since 10th November. Net outflows went between $12-$33 million over the past week, including about $21 million on the 16th alone!

Not too long ago, it was the other way around.

In August, XRP went up by about 72% and back above $1.50. Whales were dumping as much as $75 million on Binance in a single day!

If you look further back, you’ll see that XRP hit $3.55 in the summer of 2025. In that time, some days saw more than $100 million flood in.

One day even hit close to $270 million.

When coins leave an exchange, people usually want to hold. However, don’t get excited yet. Some of this might just be Binance moving its money around.

Remember when it was topping up its reserves after the October hack?

Lowest weekly close in two years…

data.title: Solana Foundation takes ‘majority interest’ in CoinGecko – What changes next?
data.description:
The Solana Foundation now holds a “majority interest” in CoinGecko, its Chief Product Officer Vibhu Norby said on X.

CoinGecko described the arrangement as “backing” when it announced the news at Breakpoint in London on the 17th of November. Neither announcement gave the exact stake, price, or governance terms.

Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted independent ownership as a reason to choose its data service over Binance-owned CoinMarketCap. It now plans to explore trading alongside its market data.

Could users trade directly on CoinGecko?

The Foundation said it planned to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko’s website, app, and GeckoTerminal. Notably, CoinGecko said it was still exploring trading features.

For Solana, that could mean reaching traders where they already look up prices. CoinGecko draws well over 50 million monthly sessions, according to the Foundation.

On the 17th of November, Solana [SOL] recorded $50.44 billion in 30-day DEX spot volume, whereas Ethereum [ETH] recorded $53.86 billion.

Norby also flagged broader coverage of stocks and real-world assets [RWAs]. AMBCrypto reported that Solana’s RWA value reached $5 billion in October.

By the 12th of November, tokenized equity supply stood at $607 million, with xStocks accounting for 75%.

Who sets CoinGecko’s data rules?

CoinGecko’s API guide warned that exchange ownership could raise questions about bias in rankings and trading volumes. AMBCrypto covered similar concerns when Binance bought CoinMarketCap in 2020.

After Norby’s disclosure, an X user called the new arrangement “a credibility problem.”

CoinGecko said its methods would stay “transparent, publicly accessible.” Readers can check how it calculates prices, but the announcements leave open who can approve changes to those rules.

Brera Holdings disclosed board rights in a separate 2025 deal involving Solmate. A later filing specified that the Foundation could nominate up to two directors, depending on board size. For CoinGecko, board seats and approval rights remain undisclosed.

Final Summary

  • The Solana Foundation, according to its product chief, Vibhu Norby. Four days earlier, CoinGecko had promoted its independent ownership.
  • They plan to add Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko. CoinGecko says the rules it uses to calculate prices will stay public.

data.title: Bitcoin tests $62K support – Can BTC bulls hold without Spot demand?
data.description:
After the $3 billion crypto liquidation wave that occurred on the 13th and 14th of November, the liquidation numbers have slowed slightly.

A relatively small liquidation number of just over $563 million was recorded on the 15th, and just $289.9 million in liquidations across the market on the 16th of November, according to CoinGlass data.

AMBCrypto reported recently that the Bitcoin [BTC] price move down to $62k acted as a leverage flush. It remains to be seen whether the bulls can enforce a recovery from here.

THIS supply cluster could keep BTC’s revival hopes alive

In a post on X, Glassnode showed that the price was trading just above a dense cluster of short-term holder supply. The darker cells denote more BTC supply in STH custody at that cost basis.

The $62k-$63k area was a particularly dense STH supply cluster, and in recent days, there has been a positive reaction. The same area had been the base of the previous impulse move higher in mid-August.

If this area is breached, it could lead to another capitulation and new lows being formed.

Sustained demand is necessary to stabilize Bitcoin price trends

Crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. noted that the bulls were trying to push BTC prices higher in the futures market. The hourly taker buy-sell imbalance reached +8,709 BTC on Monday, the 16th of November.

Yet, the price was yet to push higher. The first areas of interest were the imbalance at $66.2k-$66.9k and the local high at $70,214.

Deeply negative apparent demand (30-day sum), with a 30-day reading of -247,700 BTC and a yearly measurement of -1.21 million BTC, highlighted severe market stress.

Crypto analyst Darkfost wrote that the metric, which is an indirect on-chain proxy based on new issuance versus changes in supply inactive for over a year, does not measure net cash outflows.

Nevertheless, it has historically been a reliable indicator that helps confirm trend strength. Right now, any price rebound without apparent demand easing toward neutral or positive levels would signal weakness.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin price sank to $62k, a dense pocket of short-term holder supply, and has managed to bounce to $65k in the past 48 hours.
  • There is short-term futures demand, but sustained demand is lacking and continues to signal buyer weakness.

data.title: Here’s how Ledger’s website was hit by the Optimizely malware attack
data.description:
On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

How was Ledger’s website affected?

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely said,

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

How much crypto did victims lose?

Report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,

Most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

What happened at Polymarket?

A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

Polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company said it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

Final Summary

  • Ledger’s website served malware in an attack that reached 178 organizations.
  • However, losses among Ledger visitors remain unknown.

data.title: XRP price’s plan to break past $1 depends on ETF flows, sentiment, and…
data.description:
At press time, XRP seemed to be attempting to stage a short-term recovery on the 4-hour chart. Unfortunately, persistent institutional outflows and a critical technical hurdle at the $1.00-level have been keeping the altcoin’s bullish hopes in check.

ETF flows show sustained bleeding

As per data for 17th November, U.S Spot XRP ETFs saw net outflows of $6.14 million. This bleeding was mainly concentrated in two products — The Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) saw $5.01 million leave the fund, while the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) recorded outflows of $1.12 million.

These outflows were in line with XRP Spot ETFs’ broader trend. For the uninitiated, the week ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million — the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

That’s not all either as the recent exodus also hinted at a lack of institutional conviction around XRP’s press time price levels.

A visible short-term bounce?

AMBCrypto’s look at XRP’s 4-hour chart hinted at the altcoin showing signs of life following a steep downtrend that bottomed out near $0.89 on 15th November.

At the time of writing, the price was hovering at $0.9979 after having been rejected from its 24-hour high of $1.0078.

However, momentum indicators appeared to be turning positive. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) had crossed above the neutral line, sitting at 55.19 at press time. This implied that buyers were regaining control.

Furthermore, the MACD registered a bullish crossover, with the histogram flashing green bars — a signal that short-term momentum may be shifting to the upside.

XRP price prediction: A make-or-break moment?

The 4-hour chart recorded XRP struggling to break the $1.00-$1.01 psychological barrier, in line with the top of its recent consolidation.

If XRP can secure a 4-hour close above $1.0078, it would confirm a short-term breakout. Its next target will then be $1.05, followed by $1.09.

And yet, it is likely that XRP can face a rejection at $1.00. This will then cause a retest of the $0.95 support zone. Conversely, a break below $0.94 would expose $0.89 to further falls.

Conclusion

XRP’s 4-hour MACD and RSI hinted at a relief rally. On the contrary, XRP’s $6.1 million ETF outflows and its hard resistance at $1.00 suggested that traders should still remain cautious.

In the short term, unless XRP can close above $1.01, it will remain vulnerable to a pullback.

Final Summary

  • U.S Spot XRP ETFs recorded 6.14 million in outflows on 17th November as institutional sell-offs continued.
  • XRP must close above the $1.01 resistance to break out towards $1.05.

data.title: Glassnode flags mounting capitulation and realized losses across Bitcoin markets
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] traders were down nearly 20% on average. In general, bull market corrections form a bottom at 12% in unrealized losses for the average active trader.

This level of unrealized losses has historically come alongside bottom formations, though it could take at least two months before making a reliable recovery.

Bitcoin holders realized a net loss of 25.8k BTC during the recent sell-off, according to the crypto intelligence platform CryptoQuant. This was the largest 1-day net loss reading since the 13th of July.

The metric uses the price of the coin’s acquisition versus the price at which it was last moved to compute net profit or loss. In early November, the previously positive readings flipped, showing holders were realizing losses.

As Bitcoin prices fell, the net realized losses grew, indicative of investors selling at greater losses. This behavior is commonly seen during bear market phases.

Demand growth contracts at the fastest pace since July

AMBCrypto reported that the leverage flush that led to nearly $3 billion in long liquidations last week might be over, due to the decline in Open Interest.

The importance of sustained demand for a BTC recovery cannot be overstated. However, the market is still in deeply unfavorable conditions for buyers.

The demand growth metric was contracting at a rapid pace, the fastest since early July. The 30-day futures demand growth had been positive in October, but has faded since. The spot demand growth has been negative since the peak in mid-August.

Increased liquidations hastened the perpetuals futures demand contraction, and bearish market sentiment meant the combined total demand growth metric’s 30-day average was -400k BTC.

There were few buyers to absorb the supply being sold.

Capitulation has set in; bulls battle to defend August block

Glassnode presented evidence that spikes in realized losses mirrored past Bitcoin bear markets and represented capitulation episodes. Increased loss-selling has accompanied the sweep of a considerable magnetic zone of liquidations, from $59.5k-$62.2k.

The $62k-$66k block represented a zone where a fifth of the coins in short-term holders’ hands was acquired. The price is already well below the STH cost basis at $74.1k, where recent buyers would be at break-even.

A daily session close below $62k would mean more panic among STH. This could transform a bearish break into a rout, Glassnode warned, making the current block the support bulls must defend.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin unrealized losses for active traders were at -20%, well below the expected 12% drawdown in a bull market correction.
  • The Bitcoin short-term holder cost basis at $74.1k and the $62k-$66k August block were the two pivotal price regions investors should watch.

data.title: Assessing why Monero crypto’s price slipped below $500 despite major audit news
data.description:
A week ago, MAGIC Grants, the non-profit cryptocurrency research, funding, and blockchain charity, contracted zkSecurity to review the generalized bulletproofs implementation in Monero [XMR] for the Full-Chain Membership Proofs (FCMP++). Monero announced that the audit had been successful, quoting MAGIC Grants’ published findings. It announced that,

“It proves that the Generalized Bulletproofs protocol, in the form Monero implements it, is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound.”

No high or medium severity issues

zkSecurity reviewed the code alongside the cryptography for Generalized Proofs. Commissioned to examine the Generalized Proofs crate within the Monero Oxide project, the audit found no high or medium severity issues.

Four low-severity issues and three informational findings were reported, which the project developers have responded to since.

Generalized Proofs powers the FCMP++ upgrade, a major privacy upgrade for Monero. They are extensions of the standard Bulletproofs zero-knowledge protocol and are modified to support Pedersen vector commitments.

After the code review, zkSecurity wrote a separate proof of the protocol’s security in the Lean theorem prover, which builds machine-checkable mathematical proofs. This independent formalization proved the completeness of the Generalized Proofs protocol in the form Monero currently implements.

Impact on XMR’s price action

The sweep of the late 2025 highs around $600 did not result in a bullish breakout. Instead, the previous week’s sell-off saw XMR close the weekly trading session below $500.

This was only a reset within the broader uptrend the privacy token has enjoyed since 2025. However, the reset could go deeper, below $500. The $390-$440 demand zone was the closest on the weekly chart.

Zooming in, the 4-hour chart showed a short-term selling opportunity. The bearish impulse move to $455 was followed by a bounce to $518, the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level. XMR slid back towards $500 in the last 24 hours.

This reaction may be a sign that the sellers were back in control, with the DMI’s downtrend highlighting that this could continue.

Final Summary

  • zkSecurity found the Generalized Proofs protocol, in the form Monero implements, “is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound.”
  • XMR has enjoyed a multi-year uptrend, with the recent retracement only part of that uptrend.

data.title: XRP loses August swing low, but here’s why its price could bottom near $0.78
data.description:
XRP has been deeply affected by the crypto market’s sell-offs in recent weeks. Towards the end of September, when Bitcoin [BTC] was challenging the $87K resistance level, XRP bulls were trying to establish a foothold above the $1.50 supply zone.

They pushed the price as high as $1.65, but could not go any higher. The subsequent selling, fueled by fear and cascading liquidation waves, has driven XRP back below a swing low that is both technically and psychologically important.

XRP faces bearish price structure shift, while an analyst called a market bottom

XRP’s bullish price structure shift in August (green) originated at the swing low at $0.99 (orange). The same low was breached during the selling in recent weeks.

The CMF slipped below -0.05 to signal heavy capital outflows earlier in November. The Awesome Oscillator was also well below the zero line, highlighting intense southbound momentum.

Against this bearish backdrop on the daily timeframe, crypto analyst and trader Ali Martinez posted an encouraging chart. The weekly timeframe has formed an ascending triangle pattern over the past five years.

The rising trendline of the triangle is about to be tested, and could be the long-term bottom. His prediction suggested that the current dip could extend to $0.78.

Here, it’s worth noting that the analyst’s call for a market bottom was accompanied by net buying on Coinbase. As well as a TD Sequential buy signal on the daily timeframe.

XRP price prediction — Look to sell the bounce!

The 4-hour chart was also bearish alongside the daily timeframe. The drop to $0.893 saw a bounce to $0.95 in just few days. The CMF also moved into neutral territory, while the Awesome Oscillator’s green histogram bars suggested that bearish momentum was weak.

A price move above $1.0 would be an indication of a corrective bounce. Such a bounce is likely to reach $1.13 and $1.28, the notable imbalances overhead. This would also happen to align somewhat well with the Fibonacci retracement levels.

Final Summary

  • XRP might be approaching a long-term rising trendline support around $0.78, which could mark a market bottom.
  • Short-term bias for the altcoin has been bearish, and traders can look to sell a bounce towards $1.13-$1.28.

data.title: Zcash price eyes $940 – Can ZEC turn its relief rally into a recovery?
data.description:
Zcash [ZEC] has been moving against the grain of the broader crypto market, gaining 2.86% over the past 24 hours while Bitcoin [BTC] slipped 0.07% and the overall market continued to trade flat. This suggested the recovery was specific to ZEC rather than a result of improving market-wide sentiment.

However, the rebound came after a steep correction, as ZEC is down 19.85% over the past seven days. With no fresh catalyst to explain the move, the gains seem to be a short-term relief rally. The question now is whether buyers can sustain this recovery.

Can Zcash hold its daily recovery?

On the daily chart, bulls have started fighting back as short-term momentum picks up. At the time of writing, ZEC traded at $921.75, remaining within the lowest Fibonacci retracement band. This indicated that the recovery was still weak and left the broader bearish structure intact.

OBV showed a modest uptick after its sharp decline, while the RSI climbed to 35.41, suggesting selling pressure had eased but not enough for buyers to gain the upper hand in the market.

Zcash approaches a key H4 resistance level

The H4 chart offered a closer look at the token’s recent recovery, with ZEC trending towards the 23.6% Fibonacci level at $939.93. If the bulls can successfully break above this resistance, it would strengthen the bullish case and bring the daily $1,013 level into focus.

The MACD turned positive, while OBV began to stabilize after its steep decline. However, the lack of a stronger OBV recovery suggests buying volume has yet to fully support the improving momentum.

Final Summary

  • Zcash’s short-term recovery is gaining traction, but the daily chart shows that the broader bearish structure remains intact.
  • Holding above $906 and breaking the $939-$940 resistance could open the way towards $945-$971.
